{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: This is a Flux-native batch script intended to be run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Resources (from Slurm)
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks=1
#   --mem=6gb
#   --time=20:00:00
#   --job-name=HEPG2_rna_seq
#   --output=nextflow.out
#   --error=nextflow.err
#   --mail-type=END,FAIL
#   --mail-user=john.rinn@colorado.edu
#   -p long

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=20h
#flux: --job-name=HEPG2_rna_seq
#flux: --output=nextflow.out
#flux: --error=nextflow.err

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=6gb
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally available as a portable directive.
# Performance implication: the job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or heavy swapping.

# Omitted Slurm option: -p long (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on a different class of nodes than intended, affecting wait time and performance or causing policy rejection.

# Omitted Slurm options: --mail-type=END,FAIL and --mail-user=...
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: no automatic completion/failure emails; monitoring must be done via Flux tools/logs.

pwd; hostname; date
# SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE is not set under Flux; avoid relying on it.
echo "Here we go."

module load singularity/3.1.1

nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq -r 1.4.2 \
  -resume \
  -profile singularity \
  --reads '/scratch/Shares/rinnclass/CLASS_2022/JR/CLASS_2022/class_exeRcises/analysis/17_API_RNASEQ/fastq/*{_read1,_read2}.fastq.gz' \
  --fasta /scratch/Shares/rinnclass/CLASS_2022/data/genomes/GRCh38.p13.genome.fa \
  --gtf /scratch/Shares/rinnclass/CLASS_2022/data/gencode.v32.annotation.gtf \
  --pseudo_aligner salmon \
  --gencode \
  --email john.rinn@colorado.edu \
  -c nextflow.config

date
"
}
